sections.h2: Who handles a Saginaw County tax bill
sections.html:
Saginaw County splits the work among three desks. Value comes from your city or township assessor, the first bill from that municipality's treasurer, and any overdue balance from the county. Assessing stays local across Michigan, so the name and number on your notice get you an answer quicker than a call to the county.

The County Treasurer is in Room 107 at 111 S. Michigan in Saginaw (48602), phone (989) 790-5225, open 8:00 to 5:00 on weekdays. That office collects every delinquent real property bill. It also runs the Delinquent Tax Revolving Fund and the county's hotel and motel tax, and its treasurer chairs the Land Bank Authority that holds tax foreclosed parcels. The ordinary summer and winter deadlines are local too. Ask your own municipality's treasurer.

  • Value, exemptions and the spring appeal: your local assessor.
  • Current bills: the local treasurer named on the statement.
  • Past-due balances and tax certificates: the county treasurer, (989) 790-5225.
  • Deed recording: the register of deeds, (989) 790-5270.

The 2020 census recorded 190,124 residents in 78,442 households and 85,953 housing units. About 8.7% of those units were empty, and owners held 70.5% of occupied homes. A parcel's school district changes the bill, so name the district when you list. The county mixes platted city lots in Saginaw and Frankenmuth with rural townships and riverfront land, and each of those is assessed by a different local office.

Because the county covers so many separate taxing units, two homes with similar prices can have quite different bills. The millage depends on the city or township, the school district and other local levies. When a buyer asks what taxes will run, point them to the local treasurer for the rate that applies to your exact parcel, and share your own recent statement as a starting point.

Michigan sets assessments at half of true cash value. The number the millage is applied to is taxable value. It rises every year by the lesser of 5% or inflation, and only a sale lifts it back up (MCL 211.27a). Both figures appear on the assessment notice, so compare them before deciding if an appeal is worth the effort.

Each local board of review opens on the second Monday of March and must sit at least 12 hours during that week, with evening time included (MCL 211.30). A written ruling follows before the first Monday of June, and it explains the next step to the Michigan Tax Tribunal. A township or city can also allow protests by letter, and a nonresident owner can file by letter regardless.

Some units hold extra sessions later in the year, which matters if you spot an error after the spring window closes. To build a case, collect the notice, a recent appraisal if you have one, and photos of defects like a bad roof or a cracked foundation. If the board says no, its written ruling points you to the Michigan Tax Tribunal. That step has a short clock, so read the ruling when it arrives.

Michigan boards of review
BoardWhen it meetsWhat it can do
MarchOpens the second Monday of MarchVerifies the current year's roll and hears appeals
JulyMay meet the Tuesday after the third Monday in JulyCorrects qualified errors for the current and one prior year
DecemberMay meet the Tuesday after the second Monday in DecemberMakes the same qualified error corrections

The July and December boards sit only when there are errors to fix or hardship exemptions to weigh, and every board can rule on exemption applications for the current year. Each local unit sets its own schedule, so check with your assessor before you count on a date.

Overdue real property tax can be settled in person, by mail or online. At the counter, bring cash, a money order or a certified check. A personal check is accepted only for a first-year delinquency paid before January 1. Visa, MasterCard and Discover are taken. Mail goes to Saginaw County Treasurer, 111 S. Michigan Avenue, Saginaw, MI 48602.

The web option runs at all hours through an outside vendor, which charges an access fee on the whole payment. The card rules are strict:

  • A government photo ID must accompany a card payment, and the card must carry the payer's name.
  • If a payment is reversed or declined, it is treated as void and all fees, interest and forfeiture fees reapply from the original date.
  • A voided payment that had a redemption certificate recorded adds $20 for the correction.
  • An overpayment below $3 is absorbed into interest, and larger refunds return to the same card.
  • Payments post to the parcel you name, and there is no refund for paying the wrong parcel.

Confirm the parcel number before you submit, particularly if you own several lots, because a wrong-parcel payment stays wrong.

sections.h2: Does selling reset the tax bill?
sections.html:
Yes. Come the following year, taxable value is raised to state equalized value, and the new owner has 45 days to file the transfer with the local assessor on a state form. Not every transfer counts. Spouses, a parent, child or grandchild taking a home they will not use commercially, and some trust and foreclosure transfers are treated as no change of ownership.

Anyone shopping by monthly payment should hear this early. Your capped bill does not follow the house, so the first bill under new ownership can land well above yours. Hand the buyer's agent a recent statement and expect fewer questions later.

Before the register will take a warranty deed, the Treasurer must issue a certificate: $5 for the first five descriptions, $1 for each additional one. It rests on proof that the previous five years of taxes are paid (MCL 211.135). A quitclaim deed carrying no warranty skips it.

With any year delinquent, ask the Treasurer for a payoff in writing before settling on a closing date. Interest and forfeiture fees change the total, so a number quoted by phone goes stale. The title company can then pay the balance from your proceeds.

Here is a workable order of operations:

  1. Check the current bill with your local treasurer and earlier years with the County Treasurer.
  2. Get the payoff in writing.
  3. Warn the title company if the deed will warrant title, so the certificate is ordered.
  4. Prompt the buyer to file the sale with the assessor.
  5. Call (989) 790-5270 to ask how the deed will be filed.

Both the Treasurer and the Register of Deeds are in the courthouse on S. Michigan Avenue, which lets one visit cover the certificate and the filing. Out-of-state owners can do most of this by phone and mail.

faqs.q: Who mails my Saginaw County property tax bill?
faqs.a: The treasurer of your city or township sends it. Once real property tax is delinquent, call the County Treasurer at (989) 790-5225.

faqs.q: When do Saginaw County appeals open each year?
faqs.a: Boards open the second Monday of March and sit through that week. Your assessor's office has the exact schedule.

faqs.q: Can I pay past-due Saginaw County tax online?
faqs.a: Yes, around the clock through an outside vendor that adds an access fee. Cards paid at the counter need the payer's government photo ID.

faqs.q: Will a sale raise the next tax bill?
faqs.a: It can. The next year taxable value moves to state equalized value, and the buyer has 45 days to report the transfer.

faqs.q: Where do I get a certificate for a warranty deed?
faqs.a: Go to the County Treasurer, Room 107 of the courthouse. It costs $5 for up to five descriptions, then $1 each.
